summary: PASS 23/23 pytest on the postseason-schedule fallback fix (test_postseason_schedule_fix.py). Bug resolved: /api/teams/status?teams=MLB:NYY now returns highlight='today', label='Today vs BOS' (postseason Wild Card game surfaced via ESPN teams/{abbr}/schedule endpoint, seasonType=3) instead of the previous 'offseason/No games scheduled'. NFL:DAL — which previously wrongly showed offseason because its nextEvent held a stale Final — now correctly returns highlight='soon', label='Oct 4 @ HOU'. Verified all 6 in-season/postseason teams (MLB:NYY|MLB:LAD|NFL:DAL|NFL:KC|NBA:LAL|NHL:BOS): NONE return 'offseason'; each has a valid live/today/soon/upcoming highlight from the schedule endpoint. Score/oppScore pairing invariant enforced (both null OR both numeric). Stale-game invariant enforced: no 'recent' 0-0 leaks, and any 'recent' highlight is verified to have a date within ±14h via server._hours_since. Direct unit call of the new _next_event_from_schedule('baseball','mlb','NYY') and ('football','nfl','DAL') helper returns non-None events with valid date+state. /api/device/scores compact shape {t:[{c,s,o,h,l,r}]} verified with s/o both null when h != live|recent. Regression PASS: /api/weather/current (temp numeric, in-range), /api/device/folly (dir in {in,out,null}), /api/device/lake ({lvl,tgt,full,w}).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py _next_event_from_schedule() (lines 588-614): correctly hits site.api.espn.com/.../teams/{abbr}/schedule which returns BOTH regular season (seasonType 2) and postseason (seasonType 3) events in a single chronological list. Iterates events, returns immediately on state=='in' (live wins), otherwise picks the first event whose _hours_since ≤ 14 (i.e. current/next). Falls through to None only if the whole schedule is >14h old — genuine offseason. Robust exception handling returns None on network failure.

server.py _team_status_one() lines 703-716: order-of-fallback is correct — try nextEvent[0] first (fast common path); if that event is state=='post' and older than 14h, discard it and consult the schedule helper. This means the schedule helper only fires when needed (schedule endpoint is heavier), keeping p95 low.

The fix preserves the score-nulling invariant from iteration 13: when the resolved event is NOT a recent_final (14h window + real scores), data['score'] and data['oppScore'] are forced to null before choosing today/soon/upcoming. Verified live: NYY's today game returns score:null, oppScore:null.

Team-status cache (_team_cache TTL=120s) applies AFTER the whole resolution, so the schedule-endpoint fallback is also cached — this is desirable (avoids hammering ESPN). A test needing immediate re-evaluation would need to wait ≤120s.
Minor deprecation: server.py still uses @app.on_event('shutdown'); FastAPI recommends lifespan handlers. Non-blocking, but worth cleaning up in a future pass.

rca_of_issue: Root cause: ESPN's /teams/{abbr} endpoint returns a `nextEvent` field that (a) is often EMPTY during the regular-season→postseason gap, and (b) even when populated, only covers regular-season events (seasonType=2) — it does NOT surface playoff/World Series/Super Bowl games (seasonType=3). Previously, when nextEvent was empty OR pointed at a stale finished game, _team_status_one fell through to `highlight='offseason', label='No games scheduled'` — wrongly claiming a postseason team had nothing on the schedule. Fix (verified): new _next_event_from_schedule() calls the /teams/{abbr}/schedule endpoint (which INCLUDES all season types 1/2/3) and returns the live game, soonest upcoming event, or a still-fresh (≤14h) final. _team_status_one now consults this helper whenever nextEvent is empty or is a stale post-state event. Live confirmation: NYY now returns 'Today vs BOS' (postseason WC game), DAL returns 'Oct 4 @ HOU' — matching the requested behaviour across MLB/NFL/NBA/NHL.
